strengths: Principled and innovative data generation framework: The evolutionary discovery pipeline (skew-product recombination, parameter perturbation, and systematic filtering via the 0-1 test, recurrence checks, and Lyapunov exponents) is an elegant solution to the data scarcity problem in nonlinear dynamical systems.

Strong architecture-grounding in dynamical systems theory: The integration of dynamic mode decomposition / Koopman-inspired embeddings (polynomial and random Fourier features) alongside interleaved temporal and channel attention directly addresses the physical requirements of coupled differential equations.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Strong zero-shot generalization across 9,300 held-out synthetic chaotic systems, three real-world experimental dynamical datasets (double pendulum, C. elegans eigenworms, coupled circuit network), and surprising zero-shot transfer to chaotic PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street).

Insightful mechanistic analysis: The discovery of an attractor-diversity scaling law (keeping total timepoints fixed while scaling unique dynamical systems) and the frequency-probing showing emergent nonlinear resonance patterns in cross-channel attention heads offer genuine scientific insights beyond standard benchmark reporting.
weaknesses: Figure legibility and visual presentation: Several key figures (notably Figures 2, 4, 5, and 8) have small axes labels, legends, and inset text that are difficult to read without high zoom.

Scope of SciML baselines: The evaluated baselines are primarily general-purpose time-series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE). While Chronos-SFT provides an in-domain baseline, comparisons against continuous-time or operator-learning architectures (e.g., neural ODEs, FPO/Poseidon variants, or reservoir computers) on the experimental and PDE benchmarks would provide further context.

Unresolved trade-off with MLM pretraining: The ablation studies show that while masked language modeling (MLM) improves one-step or masked completion performance, it degrades autoregressive rollout accuracy. While acknowledged in the limitations, further analysis or discussion on why this occurs would be valuable.

Details on temporal normalization and discretization: Chaotic continuous-time systems depend heavily on the sampling timescale $\Delta t$. Providing clearer discussion on how temporal discretization, scaling, and non-dimensionalization are handled when deploying zero-shot on experimental data and PDEs would enhance reproducibility.

strengths: Compelling conceptual framing and ambition: The paper addresses out-of-domain generalization in scientific machine learning by building a universal pretrained model (Panda) tailored to chaotic dynamical systems rather than generic time series.

Principled dataset generation: Generating 20,000 distinct chaotic ODEs via evolutionary mutation and skew-product recombination, coupled with rigorous chaos filtering (0-1 test, Lyapunov exponent estimation, power spectra, recurrence tests), provides a high-quality synthetic pretraining resource.

Dynamics-grounded architecture: The architecture is thoughtfully designed around nonlinear dynamics principles, incorporating Takens-motivated patching, Koopman/eDMD-inspired dynamics embeddings (random polynomial and Fourier features), and interleaved cross-channel attention to capture dynamical couplings.

Strong empirical zero-shot transfer: Panda demonstrates superior zero-shot forecasting against competitive foundation baselines (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE) on 9,300 held-out synthetic systems, real-world physical/biological experiments (double pendulum, C. elegans eigenworms, coupled chaotic circuits), and even zero-shot transfer to chaotic PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex streets).

Insightful scaling law and interpretability: Demonstrating a neural scaling law specifically with respect to dynamical diversity (number of unique attractors/systems rather than just token count) is a significant scientific finding. Probing the attention maps with two-tone sinusoids reveals emergent nonlinear resonance signatures analogous to Arnold tongues and bispectral interactions.
weaknesses: Lack of domain-specific dynamical baselines: While Panda is evaluated against leading general-purpose time series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE), comparisons against specialized dynamical forecasting baselines (e.g., Next-Generation Reservoir Computers (NGRC), Neural ODEs, or Operator Learning architectures adapted for multi-system contexts) on the experimental benchmarks are missing.

Clarity on high-dimensional PDE input formatting: Training is conducted strictly on trajectories with 3 sampled channels, yet zero-shot evaluation is performed on 64-mode KS and 2D VKVS fluid flow vorticity fields. The manuscript would benefit from clearer explanations in the main text regarding how spatial coordinates/modes are mapped to channels and how full channel attention scales computationally when $C$ becomes large.

Rollout degradation under MLM pretraining: The authors observe that masked language modeling (MLM) pretraining improves fixed-horizon accuracy but degrades long-horizon autoregressive rollout performance. While acknowledged honestly as a limitation, deeper analysis or exploration of rollout-preserving objectives would strengthen the foundation model perspective.

Attractor climate/invariant measure preservation: Evaluation is primarily focused on short-to-medium term pointwise metrics (sMAPE, MAE, Spearman correlation). Additional quantitative evaluation of long-term climate statistics (e.g., empirical invariant density distance, Lyapunov spectra recovery over long rollouts) would further solidify its utility for dynamical systems.

strengths: Compelling conceptual motivation: Bridging the gap between time-series foundation models and scientific machine learning by leveraging mathematical invariants of chaotic dynamical systems (channel coupling, attractor geometry, dynamic mode decomposition).

Principled synthetic data engine: Constructing a diverse dataset of 20,000 chaotic ODEs via parameter perturbation, skew-product recombination, and multi-stage filtering (divergence culling, 0-1 chaos test, Lyapunov estimation, recurrence tests).

Thoughtful architectural modifications: Interleaving temporal attention with channel attention to handle variable inter-dependencies, combined with polynomial and random Fourier feature embeddings grounded in Koopman operator theory.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Demonstrates competitive zero-shot forecasting against strong foundation baselines (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE) on thousands of held-out ODEs, real-world experimental benchmarks (double pendulum, C. elegans locomotion, coupled electronic oscillators), and zero-shot out-of-domain transfer to chaotic PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street).

Insightful scaling law and interpretability analyses: Isolates the impact of attractor diversity (varying the number of unique systems vs. initial conditions while fixing total token count) and probes internal attention representations via frequency response and attention rollout entropy.
weaknesses: Baseline selection focused heavily on general time-series models: Comparisons are predominantly against statistical/time-series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE). The paper would be significantly strengthened by comparing against or discussing specialized dynamical system foundation baselines or neural operator / reservoir computing benchmarks designed for chaotic flow prediction.

Component interactions and negative ablation results: As shown in Figure 3 and Section 5.1, MLM pretraining combined with the dynamic mode embedding leads to degraded performance compared to using either alone, and MLM impairs autoregressive rollout. While the authors transparently report this, it suggests that the proposed inductive biases do not yet compose harmoniously.

Handling of spatial structure in PDE transfer: When forecasting PDEs (KS and von Kármán vortex street), treating spatial grid points or Fourier modes merely as permutation-equivariant channels via channel attention discards geometric/spatial locality. Clarification is needed on how channels are indexed and whether the model's channel permutation invariance limits spatial scalability.

Training-inference dimension mismatch: The model is trained strictly by subsampling trajectories to 3 channels ($d=3$), yet evaluated on higher-dimensional systems ($d > 3$). While channel attention technically permits arbitrary channel counts, training exclusively on triplets may limit the model's capacity to learn higher-order multivariate couplings.

Visual presentation and minor typographical issues: Several figures (particularly Figures 2, 4, and 8) contain very small axes, legends, and labels that are difficult to read. There are also occasional minor typos (e.g., 'exclusely' on p. 6, 'vortext' in Fig. 8 caption, 'degredation' on p. 9).

strengths: Principled and innovative dataset generation: The paper introduces an evolutionary framework using skew-product coupling, parameter mutation, and a comprehensive suite of chaos tests (0-1 chaos test, Rosenstein Lyapunov exponent estimator, recurrence tests, KPSS/ADF stationarity) to build an extensible dataset of ~20,000 diverse chaotic ODEs.

Well-motivated architecture grounded in dynamical systems theory: Patching aligns with Takens' embedding theorem, the lifted dynamics embedding (random Fourier + polynomial features) connects to extended dynamic mode decomposition (eDMD) and Koopman theory, and interleaved channel attention models deterministic coupling between coordinates.

Broad and convincing empirical validation: Evaluated across 9,300 held-out synthetic systems, real-world experimental benchmarks (double pendulum, C. elegans eigenworms, electrical oscillator network), and emergent zero-shot PDE benchmarks (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street), consistently outperforming strong baseline models.

Insightful analysis of dynamical systems scaling laws: Demonstrating that scaling the diversity of unique dynamical attractors while keeping total training timepoints fixed drives out-of-domain generalization provides a compelling insight for scientific machine learning.

Thorough evaluation of long-term attractor geometry: The paper goes beyond standard pointwise short-term error metrics (MAE/sMAPE) to evaluate invariant statistical measures, including KL divergence of trajectories, spectral Hellinger distance, and Grassberger-Procaccia correlation dimensions.
weaknesses: Limited comparison to multivariate foundation models: The primary comparisons are against univariate time series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE). While Chronos is fine-tuned on the dataset, comparing against contemporary multivariate foundation models (e.g., MOIRAI, UniTS) or scientific surrogate operators would strengthen the claim regarding architectural inductive biases.

Fixed-dimension subsampling during pretraining: In order to batch trajectories of differing state dimensions, the model randomly subsamples 3 channels during training. While practical and theoretically motivated by the minimal dimension for continuous-time deterministic chaos, this restricts the model to learning pairwise/triplet channel couplings during training, which may limit performance on complex, highly coupled multi-variable systems.

Long-horizon rollout regression to the mean: As acknowledged in Section 5.4 and Appendix M, when rolled out autoregressively beyond its trained horizon (128 timepoints), Panda tends to damp out into regression to the mean rather than maintaining sustained chaotic trajectories, highlighting an open challenge for encoder-style rollout models.

strengths: Grounding in Dynamical Systems Theory: The architecture is thoughtfully designed around fundamental concepts from dynamical systems, including Takens' embedding theorem (motivating patch tokenization), Koopman/eDMD theory (motivating polynomial and Fourier feature embeddings), and channel coupling (motivating interleaved cross-channel attention).

Principled and Rigorous Synthetic Dataset Generation: The evolutionary discovery pipeline—combining skew-product coupling with a comprehensive suite of chaos tests (0-1 chaos test, Rosenstein Lyapunov exponent estimation, near-recurrence filtering, and stationarity checks)—is a significant contribution that generates over 20,000 verified chaotic ODEs.

Convincing and Diverse Evaluation: The paper evaluates models not only on a massive held-out set of 9,300 synthetic systems, but also on real experimental benchmarks (double pendulum, C. elegans locomotion, coupled electronic circuits) and emergent transfer to infinite-dimensional PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex streets).

Evaluation Across Multiple Timescales: The study evaluates both short-term pointwise accuracy (MAE, sMAPE, Spearman) and long-term geometric invariant measures (attractor correlation dimension via Grassberger-Procaccia, KL divergence of trajectory distributions, and spectral Hellinger distance).

Insightful Scaling Laws and Probing: The paper presents an informative dynamical systems scaling law showing that model performance scales with attractor diversity (number of unique systems) rather than merely the volume of trajectory timepoints from fixed systems. Additionally, probing attention maps provides interesting insights into multiscale resonance and spatio-temporal mixing.
Computational Efficiency: Operating on multivariate patches yields a ~75x speedup in inference time over token-by-token univariate models like Chronos.
weaknesses: Channel Subsampling during Training: Batching requires subsampling trajectories to 3 channels during training (since continuous-time deterministic chaos requires at least 3 dimensions). While the model generalizes zero-shot to higher-dimensional inputs at test time, the gap between training on 3 channels and deploying on much larger channel dimensions (such as 64 PCA modes in PDE benchmarks) could benefit from more detailed analysis.

Incompatibility Between MLM Pretraining and Autoregressive Rollout: As noted in the ablations, MLM pretraining improves direct forecast/completion tasks but degrades performance during autoregressive rollout and interferes with the polynomial dynamics embedding. A deeper investigation into why masked infilling harms autoregressive stability would improve the paper.

Lack of SciML/Neural Operator Baselines for PDE Generalization: For the PDE experiments (Section 5.5), comparisons are restricted to time-series foundation models (Chronos variants). While zero-shot transfer from low-dimensional ODEs to PDEs is impressive, contextualizing against multi-physics or general PDE surrogates (even if fine-tuned or in-domain) would better calibrate the difficulty and absolute performance.

Minor Figure and Caption Inconsistencies: In Section 5.2, the text references 'Fig. 4b' when discussing the coupling strength and Pareto front, which corresponds to panel Fig. 4d. Figure 1 also exhibits slightly cramped diagram text.

strengths: Grounding in dynamical systems theory: The paper thoughtfully integrates classical nonlinear dynamics theory into neural architecture design, including Takens' delay embedding for patching, extended DMD/Koopman operator lifting for patch embeddings (random polynomial and Fourier features), and channel attention for deterministic coupling.

Principled and scalable dataset generation: The evolutionary synthesis via additive skew-product coupling over 129 curated founder systems, backed by rigorous chaoticity filters (chaos 0-1 test, Rosenstein Lyapunov exponent estimation, recurrence and stationarity tests), is a novel and valuable contribution for pretraining in SciML.

Insightful dynamical scaling law: Demonstrating that zero-shot generalization scales monotonically with the number of distinct chaotic attractors (keeping total tokens/timepoints constant) provides a clear, theory-backed insight: dynamical diversity of attractors matters far more than densely sampling trajectories from few systems.

Extensive and rigorous empirical evaluation: The paper tests both short-term pointwise accuracy (MAE, sMAPE, MSE) and invariant long-term attractor geometry (KL divergence, spectral Hellinger distance, correlation dimension, Lyapunov exponent recovery). It outperforms both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuned foundation baselines (Chronos, TimesFM, TimeMoE) with statistical significance tests provided.

Compelling generalization across modalities: Strong zero-shot transfer is demonstrated on real experimental datasets (double pendulum, C. elegans postural modes, coupled circuits) and out-of-distribution transfer to modal coefficients of PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street).
weaknesses: Rollout degradation and regression to the mean: As acknowledged in Section 5.4 and Section 6, autoregressive rollouts past the 128-step training window tend toward regression to the mean. While pointwise and distributional metrics remain favorable over baselines that 'parrot' spurious limit cycles, long-horizon attractor stability remains an open challenge under MSE training.

Training-to-inference channel mismatch: The model is trained strictly by sampling 3 channels per system for batch efficiency, yet tested on systems with higher dimensions (e.g., up to 64 modes in PDE experiments). While channel attention permits this permutation-invariant transfer, an ablation or discussion investigating how well channel interactions scale as test dimensionality significantly departs from 3 would strengthen the work.

Comparison primarily against generic time series foundation models: The primary baseline comparisons are general-purpose univariate time series models (Chronos, TimesFM, TimeMoE). While fine-tuning Chronos on the dataset (Chronos-SFT) provides a fairer benchmark, comparison against multivariate SciML multi-task/in-context baselines (e.g., ODEFormer or multi-operator surrogates adapted for forecasting) would further contextualize the architectural contributions.

Framing of PDE generalization: The PDE experiments are conducted on 64 spatial Fourier modes (KS) or 64 PCA modes (VKVS). While casting PDEs into finite-dimensional modal representations is standard in reduced-order modeling, the claim of 'emergent PDE forecasting' is effectively forecasting high-dimensional ODE state vectors rather than solving continuous-space operator formulations.

strengths: Principled Data Generation Pipeline: The evolutionary discovery pipeline for novel chaotic ODEs—leveraging parameter mutations, skew-product coupling, and rigorous filtering (0-1 chaos test, Lyapunov exponents, stationarity tests)—is novel, mathematically grounded, and solves the critical data-scarcity bottleneck in ML for dynamical systems.

Well-Motivated Dynamics-Informed Architecture: Incorporating Takens-inspired patching, Koopman/eDMD-inspired dynamics embeddings (polynomial and random Fourier features), and interleaved cross-channel attention effectively addresses the physical realities of coupled nonlinear systems.

Comprehensive and Diverse Evaluation: The paper evaluates across a wide spectrum of benchmarks: over 9,000 synthetic held-out systems, multiple real-world experimental benchmarks (double pendulum, C. elegans postural modes, coupled electronic oscillators), and zero-shot extrapolation to spatio-temporal PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street).

Insightful Scientific Analyses: The dynamical systems scaling law—demonstrating that attractor diversity is significantly more valuable than sampling additional initial conditions from fewer attractors—is an important conceptual insight for SciML. The internal representation analysis (revealing nonlinear resonance in temporal attention rollout) provides valuable interpretability.
weaknesses: Mean Regression in Extreme Rollouts: Because the model is trained with an L2-based regression objective on fixed prediction horizons, autoregressive rollout over very long horizons leads to regression toward the mean, underperforming recurrent architectures (like DynaMix) or categorical tokenized models (like Chronos) on long-term invariant statistics.

MLM Pretraining Trade-off: While masked pretraining significantly improves reconstruction/completion tasks, the authors acknowledge that it degrades long-horizon autoregressive rollout performance. This nuance slightly complicates the overall architectural recommendation.

Details of Spatial Discretization in PDE Experiments: While the zero-shot transfer from low-dimensional ODEs to infinite-dimensional PDEs is remarkable, the main text leaves out important details regarding how spatial dimensions/principal components are mapped to input channels, which is critical to properly contextualize the baseline comparisons.

strengths: Principled and novel data generation framework: The evolutionary search approach using skew-product coupling, parameter perturbation, and rigorous dynamical filtering (e.g., chaos 0-1 test, maximum Lyapunov exponent estimation, stationarity tests) addresses a primary bottleneck in SciML by synthesizing over 20,000 diverse, non-trivial chaotic systems.

Strong theoretical motivation for architectural choices: The architecture thoughtfully integrates concepts from dynamical systems theory, including Takens' embedding theorem (motivating patch tokenization), Koopman/eDMD operator lifting (motivating random polynomial and Fourier feature embeddings), and explicit cross-channel attention to capture physical coupling.

Extensive and rigorous empirical evaluation: The paper demonstrates strong zero-shot forecasting performance across 9,300 held-out ODE systems, outperforming prominent time-series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, TimeMOE) and dynamical models (DynaMix) with thorough statistical significance testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Šidák correction).

Effective zero-shot transfer to experimental data and PDEs: The model demonstrates convincing out-of-domain transfer to experimental benchmarks (double pendulum, C. elegans eigenworms, coupled electronic circuits) and an emergent zero-shot capability to forecast continuous PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex street) despite being trained strictly on low-dimensional ODEs.

Insightful analysis and interpretability: The investigation into scaling laws (isolating system diversity from total token count) and attention representations (revealing nonlinear resonance signatures and attractor recurrence structures) provides valuable scientific insights beyond standard time-series benchmarking.
weaknesses: Long-horizon mean regression: In the extreme long-horizon autoregressive rollout regime (e.g., >10× training horizon), the model is susceptible to mean regression, where recurrent architectures (like DynaMix) or tokenized generative approaches (like Chronos) show advantages in preserving certain invariant attractor measures.

Training channel constraint: Due to batching constraints across varying trajectory dimensions, training relies on randomly sampling subsets of 3 channels per system. While channel attention allows evaluation on higher-dimensional systems, it remains an open question whether joint training on full high-dimensional state spaces would significantly alter the learned representations.

Baselines on PDE forecasting: While the zero-shot PDE results are impressive, the compared operator learning baselines (FNO and DeepONet) were trained on one-step-ahead prediction with autoregressive rollout, which may compound errors faster than sequence-to-sequence surrogates.

strengths: Principled and novel data generation framework: The evolutionary algorithm combining parameter mutation, skew-product coupling, and rigorous dynamical filtering (0-1 chaos test, Lyapunov exponent estimation, stationarity tests) addresses a major bottleneck in SciML—namely, the lack of diverse, non-trivial chaotic training data.

Well-motivated architecture grounded in dynamical systems theory: Patching is linked to Takens' delay embedding theorem, lifted patch embeddings are motivated by extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (eDMD) / Koopman operator theory, and channel attention naturally captures multivariate coupling without fixing input dimensionality.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Evaluated across over 9,000 held-out synthetic systems, real-world experimental benchmarks (chaotic double pendulum, C. elegans locomotion, coupled electronic circuits), and transfer to chaotic PDEs (Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán vortex streets).

Insightful scaling law and interpretability experiments: The controlled scaling experiments demonstrate that dynamical diversity (number of unique systems) is the primary driver of out-of-domain generalization rather than trajectory length/initial conditions. Probing attention rollout via two-tone sinusoidal excitation reveals physically meaningful nonlinear resonance and recurrence structures.

Extensive ablations and supplementary validation: The authors thoroughly investigate the individual contributions of channel attention, patch sizes, lifted embeddings, and masked language modeling objectives.
weaknesses: Overstated claim regarding emergent PDE forecasting: While the zero-shot performance on Kuramoto-Sivashinsky and von Kármán flows is impressive, the PDEs are represented via modal coefficients or PCA-reduced spatial components, effectively reducing them to high-dimensional multivariate time series. Framing this as 'spontaneously developing the ability to predict partial differential equations' somewhat overstates the mechanism.

Mean regression and degradation on long-horizon rollouts: In very long autoregressive rollout regimes (e.g., L_pred > 2000), Panda suffers from regression toward the mean, underperforming recurrent architectures (like DynaMix) or tokenized discrete models (like Chronos) on geometric misalignment KL divergence (Table 15).

Suboptimal interaction between MLM pretraining and autoregressive rollout: As noted in the ablation section, while MLM pretraining improves masked completion accuracy, it degrades autoregressive forecasting rollout performance, leaving the question of an ideal unified pretraining objective partially unresolved.

Baseline comparisons for operator learning: FNO and DeepONet are trained solely in a one-step-ahead setting on limited context windows, making the baseline comparison in Section 5.4 somewhat asymmetric against multi-step autoregressive foundation models.
